terra.problem: Saying the crowd went three days with no food adds a detail. Jesus says they had been with Him three days and had nothing to eat.
“Three days with nothing to eat” presents the crowd as having gone without food for all three days. The passage does not say that.
Saying Jesus is picturing what an empty stomach does to a walker adds an unmarked account of His thoughts.
The passage says about four thousand men were present, not exactly four thousand.
The joke calls the place name a mouthful. Papa Dorin does not joke about how names sound or are said.
The passage does not say the Pharisees did not come to learn, or that they were in the same region where the crowd had been fed.
The side-dish joke does not make clear sense as a comparison: a second loaf does not establish what somebody would have as a side.
Herod's role as ruler of Galilee is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference, such as Luke 3:1.
The bread did not come out of nowhere: the disciples had seven loaves. The passage also does not say how long before this happened or that the disciples were worrying.
The passage does not say Jesus wanted the disciples to remember more than the number. He asks whether they remember and whether they understand.
Saying the twelve baskets came from just five loaves leaves out the fish. Mark 6:43 says the basketfuls contained broken pieces of bread and fish.
